title: Handcuffed man swallowed bag of drugs before death: police
article: RCMP in Surrey, B.C., say a man in their custody Thursday apparently swallowed a bag of drugs and choked before he died in hospital.
Insp. Gary Begg told CBC News on Friday the man has been identified as Brandon Whitelaw, 22, of Surrey.
RCMP officers were investigating a suspected drug house on Ravine Road in the Whalley area at around 4:30 p.m. Thursday, Begg said.
Officers spotted a vehicle with two men leaving the house and stopped it for traffic violations near 106 Avenue and 132nd Street.
Officers found narcotics inside the vehicle and arrested the two men. Whitelaw, one of the two men, began showing signs of breathing difficulty after being handcuffed, Begg said.
"Shortly after they [the officers] came into contact with the two occupants of the vehicle, they realized that one of the occupants was choking," Begg said.
Whitelaw was given emergency treatment by police, the fire department and paramedics at the scene. Paramedics recovered a small bag containing drugs in his airway, Begg said.
He was taken to Surrey Memorial Hospital but died shortly after.
"Subsequent analysis of the contents of the bag revealed it to be what we suspect is crack cocaine - 11 rocks of crack cocaine," Begg said.
An autopsy was scheduled Friday morning but the cause of Whitelaw's death has not been released.
